To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ATCA standard can be used to build a cost efficient, flexible and powerful data acquisition system for large scale experiments.

the MSADC module is a universal sampling ADC read-out system for the COMPASS experiment, which can be realized in a VME, MicroTCA or ATCA form factor and provides an interface for data, clock and trigger transfer, as well as configuration access.

the MSADC module is a very versatile and flexible building block for data acquisition systems in particle physics experiments, which can easily be adapted to different form factors and can be combined with other ADC or TDC modules to realize complete readout systems for large experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a flexible and scalable sampling ADC based read-out system for the COMPASS experiment at CERN, which can be used also for other applications.
the development of the readout system for the COMPASS experiment and with the development and application of the MSADC module in various environments.
a complete ADC based readout chain for high precision data taking experiments, which can be adapted to the specific needs of a given application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MSADC based readout electronics of COMPASS is a mature, robust and reliable system, which can be applied for various other applications.
the MSADC readout system has proved to be a very successful and reliable readout solution for many years.
the sampling ADC readout chain is a very flexible and powerful solution to realize a high performance readout system for a wide range of detectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed and built up the complete data acquisition system for COMPASS, including the frontend electronics, the ADC modules and the data acquisition system itself.
the sampling ADC readout chain is well established and provides a very stable data acquisition system for the COMPASS experiment and other applications.

the COMPASS experiment is a very successful example of how a large experiment can profit from the availability of low cost and high performance electronics components and how these components can be used to build a reliable and flexible data acquisition system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ATCA standard is an ideal platform for the development of high performance data acquisition systems.
the combination of a mezzanine based ADC module, which can be used in different form factors and a common interface standard for data and control access, allows a very flexible system design.

a modular design of the readout system is essential to allow for an easy migration to new technologies, and that the combination of data transmission, clock distribution, trigger distribution and configuration in a single serial interface is very beneficial for the overall system design.
